question: A later review of a pull request raised this finding. A rule of thumb says its text was already in the pull request a round earlier and that no earlier review had raised it. Which one is true?

bins.missed: The problem was already true at the commit the earlier review read, in the same lines, and no earlier review named that place or that behaviour. An earlier review could have raised it.
bins.made_by_fix: The text the finding points at did not change, and it was right before. It became wrong or incomplete only because of what the repair changed somewhere else.
bins.written_by_fix: The problem is in lines the repair itself wrote or rewrote, or in what the repair's own merge dropped.
bins.new_from_outside: The problem is new at this commit and the repair's own lines did not cause it. The base branch moved: the pull request now conflicts with it, no checks ran, or lines that landed on the base branch break it.
bins.raised_before: An earlier review already named the same place or the same behaviour, in other words. The repair fixed part of it or none of it.
bins.not_a_problem: It does not block. The reviewer says it is out of scope or only a note, or the text is not a finding at all: it reports that an earlier finding is fixed, or that a check passed.
bins.cannot_tell: The text and the facts given do not settle it.
